title: The 8 Levels of Salary Lies to Parents
house: A bustling metropolis where plant-people navigate high rents, corporate pressures, and family dinners under glowing digital salary displays on their foreheads.

levels.name: Mia, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 1. Level 1: 1,200 dollars a month, and my parents think I am running a tech startup. I sat at the mahogany dining table, trembling as my dad carved the roast beef. My forehead glowed a pitiful 1,200 dollars, but I lied and said I made 9,500. You are wearing thrift store clothes with that salary? You are spending money we know you do not have. Then my dad uttered this exact phrase that shattered my entire evening. We raised a liar under our own roof. My phone buzzed with an urgent notification showing my account was deeply in the red. I do not know how I will even pay my electric bill this week. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 25, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 2. Level 2: 2,400 dollars a month, serving overpriced oat lattes while my mom asks why I am not a manager yet. I handed a 7-dollar caramel macchiato to a sleek Broccoli-man with a 6,000 badge on his forehead. Is that your weekly take-home, kid? My face burned hot red behind the espresso machine as the queue behind him snickered. How can I afford a flight when my rent swallows eighty percent of my life? Then a customer dropped a folded envelope right into my tip jar with a heavy thud. You do not have to hide your truth from us anymore. I opened the envelope and found a cashiers check for five hundred dollars. Who could have possibly known about my financial struggles? You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Chloe, 28, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 3. Level 3: 4,100 dollars a month, yet I told my parents I pull in six figures at a hedge fund. I sat across from my mother at an upscale bistro, nervously sipping lemon water. My forehead proudly displayed my real 4,100 net, but I kept my bangs swept low to obscure it. Why is your number still so embarrassingly low, Chloe? I pay my own rent, buy my own groceries, and I am debt-free. Then my mother leaned across the white tablecloth and dropped a bombshell. Everyone in our family knows you are just a glorified clerk. The manager handed me a housing contract for a luxury penthouse I never requested. Your mother insisted you could easily afford the monthly down payment. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Marcus, 34, Senior Analyst
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 4. Level 4: 6,800 dollars a month, and I told my dad I bought a penthouse when I actually rent a damp basement studio. I stood in my sleek glass-walled office, loosening my tie after a grueling twelve-hour shift. My phone rang with my father's caller ID flashing on the screen. Your cousin just bought a vacation home in Aspen with his 12,000 salary. I make enough to live comfortably without your handouts. Then my father uttered the most humiliating sentence of my entire adult life. You are the biggest financial disappointment in this family. My monitor lit up with a data breach alert exposing my secret basement apartment. Look at this address, he does not live in a penthouse at all. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Sienna, 31, Marketing Director
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 5. Level 5: 9,200 dollars a month, yet I lied to my mother and said I make double that just to earn her approval. I sat in my luxurious glass penthouse overlooking the city skyline, swirling a glass of red wine. My mother stood by the floor-to-ceiling window, her 13,000 forehead badge glowing brightly under the recessed lights. Nine thousand is respectable, I suppose, but your cousin runs an entire conglomerate. I slammed my wine glass down on the marble counter, spilling crimson drops across the pristine surface. Then my mother turned around with a cold, piercing stare that froze my blood. You will never truly be successful until your number matches mine. The intercom buzzer echoed through the penthouse with an unexpected delivery notification. There is a legal notice downstairs demanding an immediate asset audit. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Julian, 36, Tech Founder
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 6. Level 6: 12,500 dollars a month, and I told my parents I sold my startup for millions just to stop their nagging. I stood in my minimalist glass-walled conference room, surrounded by venture capitalists and anxious investors. My phone buzzed incessantly with text messages from my father demanding proof of my supposed multi-million dollar exit. When are you going to buy a real estate portfolio like your sister? I make twelve thousand a month building software used by millions. Then my father uttered the devastating line that ended the phone call forever. You are a small-time failure pretending to be a giant. Federal agents suddenly entered the boardroom with freeze orders for all company assets. Mr. Julian, your startup accounts have been flagged for severe financial discrepancies. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Victoria, 40, Venture Capitalist
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 7. Level 7: 18,000 dollars a month, yet I told my aging parents I am a billionaire hedge fund owner. I stood on the private helipad of my skyscraper, the wind whipping my silk scarf around my neck. My father called me from his modest suburban kitchen, his forehead badge glowing a meager 3,500. Your brother's startup just raised fifty million. I manage a billion-dollar fund. Then my father uttered the final words that cut straight through my armor. You will never be more than a fake in a rich person's world. My tablet flashed with an emergency memo from the board regarding my forged credentials. All fund transactions have been suspended pending a criminal inquiry. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Evelyn, 50, Tech Tycoon
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying about your salary to your parents. Level 8. Level 8: 50,000 dollars a month, and I finally told my dying mother the absolute truth about my entire fabricated life. I sat beside her hospital bed in the VIP palliative suite, the rhythmic beep of the heart monitor filling the quiet room. Her forehead badge flickered weakly at 1,500, a lifetime of struggle etched into her weathered skin. We always knew you were lying, my child. The glowing digits on our foreheads never mattered to us as much as your happiness did. Then my mother used her last breath to utter the sentence that completed our entire journey. The number on your forehead was never your true worth. The lawyer stepped forward and placed a dusty wooden box on the bedside table. She kept every single artwork you ever created when you were little. Which theme of salary lies or family secrets should we explore next?
